headline: Recordings grew ears: rec/v2 captures voice
lede: The arcade's replay format learned to record the players, not just their buttons — consent-first raw audio, lined up with the game clock, live from the first online race.

notes.text: Gauntlet online races can save each player's raw voice next to the actions: a consent prompt fires before any mic opens (headsets recommended — tracks don't bleed), the answer is saved in the file, and declining just means a quiet replay.
Remote players' audio rides the existing relay unchanged — an online guest's mic reaches the host as ~6 small messages a second, each track carrying its own tick clock, no server redeployed.

Alignment is measured, not assumed: files record how far the world clock drifted from real time (a synthetic half-speed 30-minute session shows +450 s), and any pad event finds its moment in the audio within a frame.
Every contract-wired game gets local mic capture for free the moment a recording starts — while scripted harness captures keep producing clean, prompt-free v1 files.
